title: Improving Stable Speech Synthesis Post-Training with ChatScorer and Margin-Based Preference Construction
abstract: Existing post-training methods for codec-based text-to-speech (TTS) often rely on multiple automatic metrics, such as character or word error rate (CER/WER) for content consistency, speaker similarity (SIM) for speaker preservation, and their weighted combinations as reward signals. However, directly fusing heterogeneous metrics into a single scalar reward can yield weakly separated candidate scores, leading to ambiguous supervision. In this paper, we propose a new post-training framework for stable speech synthesis, which introduces ChatScorer as an auxiliary reward model and combines it with margin-based preference construction. We instantiate the proposed framework using different post-training methods, and experiments on codec-based TTS show that it reduces undesirable outputs and improves generation stability, while maintaining competitive intelligibility and speaker similarity.
relevance_note: ChatScorer reward and margin-based preference construction for codec TTS post-training; TTS training method.
